_why: One corpus, two checkers. scripts/quote_integrity.py (offline, against captured source text) and scripts/quote-match.ts (live, against the fetched page) each implement 'does this quote appear in this text', in different languages, and nothing made them agree. The ' … ' elision convention was added to the Python side on 2026-10-28 and the TypeScript side did not learn it until 2026-10-31, so for three days every one of the 23 entries carrying a marked cut would have been reported as a composite by the live gate. Both test suites load this file; a convention added to one language now fails the other language's tests until it is added there too. See docs/postmortems/2026-10-31-the-elision-convention-one-gate-never-learned.md

cases.name: html entity apostrophe on the live page
cases.quote: if you're considering starting a company, then reading this book
cases.text: If you’re considering starting a company, then reading this book
cases.why: visibleText stripped tags but never decoded entities, so a WordPress page reading 'you’re' could not match 'you're'. Ten entries — every one a blog, Substack or Goodreads page, the formats that emit entities — were reported as composites, which is the gravest verdict this checker has. LinkedIn and X are skipped by the live checker, which is why the cluster looked like a vintage rather than a format.
